data.name: charges
data.description: To charge a credit or a debit card, you create a charge object.
data.extended_description:
use `query_sigma`, or call `get_sql_template` first when `available_templates` are present.

SQL — Sigma uses Trino SQL.

TIMEZONE — every timestamp column is UTC unless the column specifically states
otherwise; the merchant's reporting timezone is
the `timezone` attribute of the most recent <message_datetime> tag. Convert filter
bounds from that timezone to UTC before comparing, and convert returned timestamps
back to it before bucketing or stating a time.

REPORTING — When you report to the user, always be explicit about the start and end
times for time-bounded queries. Make sure the user knows when the data is starting and ending.


card_country is the primary geographic signal for charge-level country attribution; used in MRR by Country as a fallback when customer.address_country and customer.shipping_address_country are both null. Join with payment_method_details on charges.id = payment_method_details.charge_id to get alternative country signals (link_country, paypal_shipping_country, etc.). outcome_risk_score and outcome_risk_level come from Radar — higher scores indicate higher fraud risk. outcome_network_decline_code contains the raw issuer decline code (e.g. 51 for insufficient funds, 05 for do not honor) useful for decline reason analysis. card_fingerprint is stable across card re-issues — use it to track a card across multiple charges even when card_last4 or card_id changes. card_address_zip_check and card_address_line1_check indicate whether the billing address matched the issuer's records.
